name: Old Rose
lede: Old rose is a muted, dusty pink, the color of a faded rose rather than a fresh one.

sections.title: A faded pink
sections.body:
Paterson defines old rose simply as a deep pink [1]. St Clair, in her list of color names, is more particular: a dusty pink with blue undertones [2]. The two definitions agree on pink and disagree on depth, which is typical for a name built on the idea of age rather than a measured shade.

The word *old* works as a modifier in several color names. Paterson notes that *old* is used with names such as gold to give the look of age, and lists old coral, old gold and old rose together [1]. Old gold, for example, is first recorded as a color term in 1879 [1]. The same dictionary lists old rose with the pinks next to peach bloom, nude and [[pink]]-family names such as damask and magnolia [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of museum paintings, a color within range of this swatch appears in 23 works, 0.1 per cent of the archive [3]. The earliest is a 1398 work in the Cleveland Museum of Art, and the latest a 1922 painting in Copenhagen [3]. No single painter dominates it [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
